title: Connection-Lifecycle — eBPF Tracer
description: Zero-instrumentation TCP connection-health metrics. All data captured via eBPF probes on tcp_v4_connect and tcp_set_state — no SDK changes required. The reset rate is the key failure signal: a burst indicates a cascading connection failure or an unhealthy dependency.

panels.title: Connection Resets / sec (the failure signal)
panels.description: Rate of TCP connections closing with a reset / handshake failure, by destination. A spike here is the signature of a cascading connection failure or a dependency going unhealthy. This is the panel to alert on.

panels.title: Connection Opens / sec by Destination
panels.description: Outbound connect() attempts per second. Compare against resets to compute a failure ratio; a rising open rate with flat establishes suggests SYN drops or a port-closed peer.

panels.title: Active In-Flight Connections
panels.description: Currently-tracked outbound connections (SYN_SENT or ESTABLISHED). A sudden drop to zero indicates mass connection failure; a steady climb without release suggests a connection leak.

panels.title: Established Connection Duration (s)
panels.description: Wall-clock open→close duration distribution. A shift toward the left (shorter durations) reveals connection churn — e.g. a missing keep-alive causing rapid reconnect cycles.

panels.title: Reset Rate (all destinations)
panels.description: Aggregate resets per second across all peers. Use as a single-number health KPI; alert when this exceeds the baseline.

panels.title: Top Destinations by Reset Count
panels.description: Which dependency is failing the most. Sort descending to find the unhealthy peer.
